capabilities: Synchronize vault files across devices via S3, WebDAV, Google Drive, or Dropbox backends
Configure per-path sync strategies with ordered glob match rules
Resolve sync conflicts using smart merge, keep both, latest survive, or keep remote/local strategies
Extend the plugin with custom backends, triggers, and strategies via the module SDK
extras: Open-source under the MIT License with stated no-telemetry claims; full documentation lives at an external site (sync.consensia.cc) covering usage, modules, permissions, and benchmarking. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: There's already a lot of plugins to sync your notes between devices
motivation: The author saw a gap for users who want to choose their own storage, keep the plugin small because unused features aren't bundled in, and get syncing no slower than a self-hosted server.
problem: Obsidian Sync is paid, and existing sync plugins are either optionally paid and stalled (Remotely Save), require running your own server (Self-hosted LiveSync), or route notes through managed infrastructure you don't control (Relay).

relations.evidence: Remotely Save supports many backends (S3, Dropbox, OneDrive, WebDAV). But is optionally paid
Self-hosted LiveSync and Fast Note Sync offer real-time, server-based sync
Self-hosted LiveSync and Fast Note Sync offer real-time, server-based sync
Relay is a managed relay service. Convenient, but your notes pass through infrastructure you don't control

summary: Vault synchronization plugin that keeps files in sync across devices via S3, WebDAV, Google Drive, or Dropbox, with encryption and an SDK for modules.
